claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy multilayers have incoherent interfaces.
Coherent interfaces can be introduced into the high-entropy alloy multilayers.
Introducing coherent interfaces will enhance the transition from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep.
Introducing coherent interfaces will improve creep resistance.
Interface coherency is the structural mediator controlling the creep response.
Facilitating dislocation movement while hindering diffusion promotes dislocation-mediated creep over diffusion-mediated creep.
Multilayers with coherent interfaces will have greater creep resistance than multilayers with incoherent interfaces.
Multilayers with coherent interfaces will have lower creep rates than multilayers with incoherent interfaces.
The proposed relationship applies to high-entropy alloy multilayers under high-temperature conditions.
The improvement in creep resistance may vary with alloy composition and interface characteristics.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation movement, whereas the predicted outcome is lower creep rate and greater creep resistance. Because easier dislocation motion would ordinarily enable deformation, the hypothesis does not coherently explain how this mechanism produces the stated outcome.
